sources.quote: Of those potential SM-80s in Texas, the TCEQ had not visited 11 of the 18, from 2017 through 2022
sources.searcher_note: OIG report 24-P-0049: TCEQ and South Coast AQMD failed to identify and inspect high-emitting synthetic-minor (SM-80) sources on the 5-year schedule. Names TCEQ, but covers synthetic minors, not Title V majors.

sources.quote: identify state-level trends in Clean Air Act enforcement data for Title V major source facilities from 2020 through 2025
sources.searcher_note: OIG project OSRE-26-0063 announced May 2026: an evaluation of state-level enforcement trends at Title V majors, 2020-2025. No findings published yet; no state named on the page.

sources.quote: In 2012, TCEQ submitted and gained EPA approval for a plan for reduced inspection frequencies for sites in three coastal regions, with major sources receiving FCEs every three years and mega sites every five years.
sources.searcher_note: Context that cuts against the lead: under an EPA-approved alternative plan, Texas coastal mega sites are only due an on-site FCE every five years. Upload path suggests Dec 2022.

sources.quote: At the beginning of the decade, the agency was conducting more than 7,500 inspections per year of federally-permitted facilities with limits on air emissions.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern only: TCEQ air inspections of federally permitted facilities fell from 7,500+ a year to about 2,000 over the 2010s. Earlier window; no 5-year-gap count.

sources.quote: potentially lead to compliance histories for some of the nearly 400,000 unclassified entities for which TCEQ currently has no compliance information
sources.searcher_note: Pattern only: the Sunset staff report says entities TCEQ has not inspected in the last five-year period are rated unclassified. Covers all media, not air majors.

sources.outlet: New Mexico legislators' letter to the Environmental Improvement Board (hosted by Western Environmental Law Center)
sources.quote: Without action, the state faces position freezes, delayed permit processing, reduced inspections, diminished monitoring, and weakened enforcement capacity.
sources.searcher_note: New Mexico context only: legislators say the Air Quality Bureau faces a funding crisis that threatens inspections. No count of overdue major-source evaluations.

notes: entity_named=yes means the page names the agency (TCEQ, or New Mexico's Air Quality Bureau). None of those pages reports the lead's finding. No source found reporting a count of Texas or New Mexico major (Title V) sources with no full compliance evaluation in 5+ years, or any per-100 rate by state. Nearest coverage is the EPA OIG SM-80 audit (TCEQ, synthetic minors, 2017-2022) and TCEQ's long inspection decline (2010s). The ECOS source shows TCEQ has EPA approval to inspect coastal mega sites only every five years, which bears on the 5-year threshold. The OIG announced a Title V state-trends evaluation in May 2026; no report found. Several PDF quotes span line breaks in the source text. The query 'Texas air pollution inspections 2026...' returned nothing dated July-September 2026.
